summary: Submitted a probe for an unexpected local result rather than asserting a claim about it. While exploring whether an equally admissible reply at the same value ballot can displace the owner's own command, the same-ballot tie-break scenario produced a state the current account does not explain: the owner's own recovery left its instance with no command (length 0, status PREACCEPTED) and emitted no proposal at all, while the recorded leader bookkeeping showed only the self reply appended and zero nacks even though three PrepareReplies had been delivered. Rather than build a finding on that, I registered it as an active question with a provisional hypothesis about the adoption loop overwriting the instance's command fields before the dispatch, and declared two comparisons that measure whether the instance keeps a command after the owner's recovery and whether the same message set delivered in a different order changes the outcome, plus the diagnostic fields (appended count, nacks, prepared flag, instance command length before and after) that the receipt will contain. The scenario, prerequisites and control (the same replies with the empty one delivered first) are declared in the experiment; no interpretation is asserted for it yet, and the five existing questions, three asserted defects, one holds account and eight knowledge entries are untouched. Remaining unfinished work: reading that receipt and explaining the observed state, including which reply the loop actually adopted.
